title: Last night's automatic patching broke image uploads
intro: Since 02:00, image uploads on the shop return HTTP 500 from app-01 (Rocky Linux 9). Nobody deployed anything, but dnf-automatic runs nightly at 02:00.

steps.prompt: Check what dnf changed recently on app-01: show the transaction history.
steps.fake_output:
ID | Command line          | Date and time    | Action(s) | Altered
57 | (dnf-automatic)       | 2026-09-28 02:00 | Upgrade   |   14
56 | install php-gd        | 2026-08-11 15:20 | Install   |    1

Transaction ID : 57
Begin time     : Sun 28 Sep 2026 02:00:14
Packages Altered:
    Upgrade  ImageMagick-libs-7.1.1.38-1.el9.x86_64 @epel
    Upgraded ImageMagick-libs-6.9.13.10-1.el9.x86_64 @@System
    Upgrade  openssl-libs-1:3.0.7-28.el9_4.x86_64 @baseos
    ...

steps.prompt: ImageMagick jumped a major version, from 6 to 7, from EPEL. Confirm in the app log that it's the cause: grep the last errors in /var/log/app/error.log.
steps.fake_output:
2026-09-28T02:04:11 ERROR upload: Imagick::readImageBlob(): no decode delegate for this image format `JPEG' @ error/constitute.c/ReadImage/741
2026-09-28T02:05:40 ERROR upload: PHP Warning: PHP Startup: Unable to load dynamic library 'imagick.so' (libMagickWand-6.Q16.so.7: cannot open shared object file)
steps.hint: Look at the error log around 02:00.

steps.prompt: The PHP extension was built against ImageMagick 6. Roll back transaction 57.
The undo also reverted the OpenSSL security fix. Re-apply the security updates now, and lock ImageMagick at version 6 so it can't jump again.
expected_commands: sudo dnf versionlock add ImageMagick-libs && sudo dnf upgrade --security -y
dnf versionlock add ImageMagick-libs && dnf upgrade --security -y
steps.fake_output:
Adding versionlock on: ImageMagick-libs-0:6.9.13.10-1.el9.*
Upgrading:
 openssl-libs  1:3.0.7-28.el9_4
Complete!
steps.hint: Lock first, then run the security-only upgrade.

steps.prompt: Restart php-fpm so it loads the working library again.
steps.fake_output: (no output: php-fpm restarted; uploads work again)

resolution: Automatic patching was set to install everything, including a major-version jump from a third-party repository (EPEL), with no staging step. ImageMagick 7 dropped the library the PHP imagick extension was linked against, so uploads broke at 02:00 with nobody watching. 'dnf history' made it a five-minute diagnosis, and 'history undo' a one-command rollback. But undo reverts a whole transaction, including the security fix that came with it, so the security updates had to be re-applied under a version lock. The better setup: automatic updates for security fixes only (dnf-automatic upgrade_type = security); major and third-party updates through a pipeline that patches staging first; and a smoke test after patching (upload an image), so failures show up at 02:05, not when customers complain.
